issues.legal_issue: A constitutional writ is not an available substitute for an ordinary civil action to enforce a private right to immovable property against private individuals, absent an alleged breach of statutory duty by a public authority.
material_facts: The dispute concerned possession and access to part of a house property between private individuals.
An eviction suit concerning the property was already pending, and an ordinary civil remedy was available for the disputed property claim.

The property owner sought writ directions against the private individuals, while also alleging that police assistance had been given to them; no breach of a statutory duty by a public authority was alleged as the basis for the property relief.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in issuing a writ direction against the private individuals. A regular civil suit, rather than a writ petition, was the appropriate remedy for the property dispute.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 226 of the Constitution, the High Court's special and extraordinary jurisdiction is not ordinarily available to settle property-right disputes between private persons or to replace remedies available under general law. A writ may be appropriate where a breach of statutory duty by a statutory authority is alleged, in which case directions may be issued to that authority. The Court referred to repeated holdings of the Supreme Court and various High Courts but identified no specific earlier case.

rule.if: constitutional_writ_petition and private_immovable_property_dispute and private_parties and ordinary_civil_remedy_available and not statutory_duty_breach_alleged

predicates.constitutional_writ_petition: A party sought relief through a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.private_immovable_property_dispute: The relief sought concerned a disputed right to or possession of immovable property.
predicates.private_parties: The property right was claimed by and against private individuals.
predicates.ordinary_civil_remedy_available: A civil remedy under the general law was available to resolve the property dispute.
predicates.statutory_duty_breach_alleged: A breach of statutory duty by a statutory authority was alleged as the basis for the requested relief.
predicates.writ_relief_unavailable: The requested writ relief is unavailable for resolving the dispute.

issues.definition: When a writ proceeding concerns a private property dispute between private individuals, an ordinary civil remedy is available, and no statutory-duty breach is alleged, writ relief is unavailable.

issues.legal_issue: Constitutional writ jurisdiction should not be used to resolve a grievance about criminal proceedings when remedies under the ordinary criminal law are available.
material_facts: The property owner alleged that the private individuals were initiating false and vexatious complaints and receiving undue police assistance.
The owner sought writ directions concerning complaints and police action, although remedies under the general criminal law were available.
issues.conclusion: Any grievance about the initiation of criminal proceedings, or orders and steps taken in them, had to be pursued through remedies under the general law, including the Code of Criminal Procedure; constitutional jurisdiction could not replace those remedies.
issues.legal_principle: Article 226 jurisdiction is special and extraordinary and should not be exercised casually or lightly to decide disputes for which ordinary civil or criminal remedies are available. A grievance about criminal proceedings and steps taken in them must be pursued under the general law, including the Code of Criminal Procedure. No specific earlier case was identified for this proposition.

predicates.constitutional_writ_petition: A party sought relief through a constitutional writ proceeding.
predicates.criminal_process_grievance: The party's grievance concerned the initiation of criminal proceedings or orders or steps taken in them.
predicates.ordinary_criminal_remedy_available: A remedy under the ordinary criminal law was available for the grievance.
predicates.ordinary_criminal_remedy_must_be_used: The grievance must be pursued through remedies under the ordinary criminal law rather than resolved through the writ proceeding.

issues.definition: When a writ proceeding concerns a grievance about criminal process and an ordinary criminal remedy is available, that remedy must be used.
